Name: Bánh Anh Em
Description: This is one of my favorite Vietnamese spots in the city. The flavors feel familiar but still fresh and modern. I like bringing friends here when I want to share a part of home with them.

Name: Whitney Museum of American Art
Description: I like coming here when I want to see something new and different. The art always feels current, and the terrace views of the city are beautiful. It’s a place that makes me slow down and think.

Name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
Description: The Met is where I go when I want to wander for hours. I love how you can walk through so many cultures and time periods in one building. It always makes the city feel bigger and more connected.

Name: 53rd Street Library
Description: This library feels like a quiet break in the middle of Midtown. I like stopping here when everything outside feels too busy. It’s calm, simple, and easy to sit and reset for a while.

Name: Tompkins Square Park
Description: This park feels very real and very local in the middle of the East Village. I’ve spent afternoons here just sitting with friends or watching people walk by. It feels like everyday New York.

Name: niconeco zakkaya
Description: A small shop full of cute and thoughtful stationery items. I like coming here when I want something simple, vintage, and thoughtful, especially for birthday postcards. It’s quiet and cozy, and it always feels intentional.

Name: Nami Nori West Village
Description: This is where I’d take someone who thinks sushi is always the same. The open-style temaki hand rolls feel fun and a little special. It’s relaxed but still feels like a treat.

Name: Tènten
Address: 119 Baxter St Unit B, New York, NY 10013
Description: A northern-style phở spot that reminds me of my hometown in the best way. The handmade noodles and lighter broth feel authentic and comforting, especially when I’m missing home. It’s one of those places that makes New York feel a little more familiar.

Name: Sorate
Description: This is a minimalist and calm tea house with a focus on refined Japanese flavors. It feels intimate and understated, which makes it perfect for slow dinners and meaningful conversations.

Name: Don Udon
Description: A comforting spot when I just want something simple and satisfying. The handmade udon feels hearty and grounding, especially on colder days. It’s a lowkey hidden spot, but it’s reliable in the best way.

Name: Tonchin New York
Description: Tonchin is usually busy, but that’s part of why I like it. The ramen feels rich and comforting after a long day. It has that lively New York energy that makes it memorable.

Name: Jing Jing Hair & Skin Care Hair Salon
Address: 34 W 36th St, 3rd floor, New York, NY 10018
Description: This is a small, local salon that feels familiar and easy. It’s not fancy, but it feels personal. I like including places like this because they show everyday life in the city.
